previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, COPD, and schizophrenia was admitted for acute respiratory distress following crack cocaine use. He presented with shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain. Imaging revealed worsening lung opacities consistent with crack-related eosinophilic pneumonia and ARDS. He developed acute on chronic systolic heart failure with pulmonary edema and required intubation and mechanical ventilation. After treatment with steroids, nebulizers, and diuresis, he improved and was extubated on hospital day 5. His diabetes was difficult to control due to steroid use but stabilized before discharge. He was evaluated by psychiatry and referred to a dual diagnosis program for substance use and mental health follow-up. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to restart home medications, monitor weight, and attend outpatient appointments.
